title: Feasibility study of a novel NK and CD8 T cells stimulating agent
text:
Cell-based therapies, whether NK or T cell-based therapies, remain challenging for solid tumors. CanCure has.
To circumvent these challenges, we have discovered a new complex molecule that can be used as an additive
during NK and antigen-specific CD8 T cell expansion to enable their superior efficacy in treating solid tumors.
The goal of this application is to select the most optimal form of the complex molecule by assaying the biological
and developmental feasibility.

title: Salivary Neural Development Programs Enable Adenoid Cystic Carcinoma Progression
text:
Adenoid cystic carcinoma (ACC) is a highly aggressive salivary gland cancer that is closely associated with
perineural invasion, yet the role of tumor innervation in its progression remains unclear. This project will create
an atlas of neuronal maps and define the patterns and functional consequences of tumor innervation in ACC
using clinical and genomic correlations, in vitro models, spatial and single nuclei transcriptomics, and patient-
derived xenograft models. By targeting tumor–nerve interactions, this research aims to uncover novel
therapeutic strategies to improve outcomes for patients with ACC.

title: Designer Red Blood Cells to Improve Transfusion Therapy
text:
Red blood cell transfusions are lifesaving but can cause serious complications, especially in patients with sickle
cell disease and premature infants. This project aims to develop a scalable source of red blood cells from human
pluripotent stem cells that are tailored for two critical clinical needs: identifying complex antibodies in transfusion-
dependent patients and providing safer, fetal-type red cells for premature neonates. These innovations have the
potential to improve transfusion safety, diagnostic accuracy, and outcomes in two high-risk patient populations.

title: POISEN: A Bioinformatics Pipeline to Identify Poison Exons in Neurodevelopment
text:
Alternative poison exon (PE) splicing is a regulatory mechanism used to rigorously maintain protein expression
across time and cell type during neurodevelopment. Pathogenic variants near PE splice sites can result in
aberrant PE splicing events that can result in severe neurodevelopmental disorders (NDDs) like genetic
epilepsy disorders, yet alternative PE splicing has been historically understudied due to the technical
challenges in identifying these alternative exons. This research proposal aims to discover PEs relevant in
human neurodevelopment and in NDD- and epilepsy-related genes by developing and applying POISEN
(Poison exOn dIScovery for long-rEad traNscriptomes), a bioinformatics pipeline that specifically detects PEs
in the long-read transcriptomes of induced pluripotent stem cell-derived cerebral organoids.

title: Repurposing esomeprazole for the treatment of scleroderma
text:
Scleroderma is a chronic disease of the connective tissue that is characterized by excessive accumulation of
fibrous material (i.e. collagen) in the skin and ultimately in the lungs and other internal organs leading to
multiple organ failure and death. Although there is no cure for this disease, research progress in animals and
humans has led to better understanding of the disease process, and possible treatment options that can halt or
reverse the disease are on the horizon. Recently, our research identified that an FDA-approved drug (for other
disease) might be effective for scleroderma, and we now propose to conduct additional studies to develop the
drug, as well as understand the mechanism(s) by which it blocks collagen accumulation in cells obtained from
scleroderma patients, and in animal models of the disease.

title: Modeling SNARE-Mediated Membrane Fusion
text:
The proposed research aims to increase our understanding of how cellular machineries accomplish regulated
exocytosis, the basis for many fundamental processes such as neurotransmitter release at neuronal synapses
which enables neurotransmission in the central nervous system. This research will contribute to understanding
mechanisms whereby synapse dysfunction leads to neurodevelopmental or neurodegenerative disorders.

title: Feedback amplification between Retrotransposons/endogenous retroviruses and TDP-43 in Alzheimers related dementias
text:
This proposal investigates the role of retrotransposons and endogenous retroviruses in
Alzheimer’s and related dementias, using a Drosophila model as well as mammalian cell
culture. The primary hypothesis that will be investigated is that retrotransposons and
endogenous retroviruses, which are virus like elements that reside in the genome, are
both upstream initiators and downstream mediators of the protein aggregation pathology
that is seen in subjects with these disorders. The proposal makes use of well
established Drosophila models of neurodegeneration that are relevant to Alzheimer’s
Related Dementias. By use of these models and of cell culture, this proposal also will
test the idea that retrotransposons and endogenous retroviruses contribute to the spread
of disease between neurons and glial cells in the brain.

title: Translation Fidelity in Hematopoietic Stem Cell Aging and Longevity
text:
Blood-forming stem cells in the bone marrow regenerate blood and immune cells throughout life. Defects in stem
cell maintenance that occur during aging lead to anemia, impaired immunity, bone marrow failure, and leukemia,
but the underlying cause of these defects is largely unknown. This proposal will examine if blood-forming stem
cell maintenance and longevity is regulated by errors in protein synthesis, and if increasing the fidelity of protein
synthesis delays onset of age-related stem cell defects and extends lifespan.

title: Determining the gastrointestinal nemabiome of sheep and goats in the USA
text:
Making informed treatment decisions for sheep and goat diseases caused by gastrointestinal worms—such as
barber-pole worms, brown stomach worms, or black scour worms—is essential for responsible anthelmintic
use and for preventing the rapid development of drug resistance. Traditional parasitological methods are
becoming less effective at identifying key species relevant to the industry, and advances in molecular
parasitology now enable us to identify the gastrointestinal nemabiome, including pathogenic worms, and to
evaluate the relative abundance of each species within individual animals. Using a standardized, cost-effective
protocol, we aim to characterize the nemabiome of small ruminants across the United States.

title: Integrating multiomic analyses for gene discovery andgenetic diagnosis of Mendelian myopathies
text:
With clinically-available genetic testing, the majority of patients with suspected monogenic muscle diseases lack
a genetic diagnosis which impedes medical management. The goal of this project is to develop best practices
for combined analysis of genome (DNA), transcriptome (RNA), and proteome (protein) research technologies to
identify novel variants and genes and improve the diagnostic yield for patients with muscle disease.

title: TR&D Project 2: AddBiomechanics for Analysis
text: High-quality personalized biomechanical simulations are needed to uncover the factors that limit mobility. Creating these simulations from movement data is a significant barrier for many researchers, including our Collaborative Projects. Add Biomechanics, a web-based tool created by the Mobilize Center, has dramatically reduced this barrier. Add Biomechanics automatically processes motion capture data to scale a musculoskeletal model to match a person and create a simulation that computes their kinematics and dynamics in less than 30 minutes, compared with about one day of manual work for a human expert. We have also demonstrated that the accuracy of AddBiomechanics is superior to expert researchers. Our aims for advancing AddBiomechanics include the following: 1. Develop cloud-based tools in AddBiomechanics to automatically estimate kinematics from inertial measurement unit (IMU) data. Users will simply drag-and-drop their data into our web-based tool to obtain accurate estimates of joint kinematics from IMU sensors. We will support data processing for a range of common movement tasks and over long durations, expanding our user community and accelerating our ability to create large movement datasets. 2. Develop machine learning methods to automatically curate large-scale movement datasets. We will use our expert-curated dataset to build a machine learning model to replace the current manual checking of AddBiomechanics. This will improve the accuracy of the data processed by AddBiomechanics and automate curation, which will allow us to develop very large, high-quality datasets. 3. Develop and validate machine learning models to accurately and rapidly estimate ground reaction forces and muscle activations and forces. We will incorporate these models in OpenCap and OpenSim to enable users to estimate unmeasured external forces and muscle dynamics in seconds rather than hours. Data processed through AddBiomechanics is automatically harmonized and shared, this will accelerate our goal to create a large-scale and high-quality movement dataset. We will leverage this dataset to build machine learning models that can estimate movement dynamics 1,000 times faster than current approaches. Through intensive interactions with our Collaborative Projects, we will focus on improving outcomes for individuals with limited mobility due to conditions such as osteoarthritis, neuromuscular diseases, limb loss, and workplace injuries.

title: Functional Dynamics and Interactions of CYP19
text:
The cytochromes P450 (CYPs) play a diverse range of roles in xenobiotic metabolism and hormone synthesis.
Among them, aromatase (CYP19) holds significant importance to human health due to its pivotal role in
converting androgens into estrogens. This research aims to unravel fundamental aspects of CYP19 function
and develop novel tools that can be applied to other CYPs and membrane proteins.

title: Mechanisms of Nociception in the Trigeminal System
text:
The proposed research will investigate the functional properties of trigeminal Aβ-afferent high-threshold
mechanoreceptors (Aβ-HTMRs), identify mechano-transducers in trigeminal Aβ-HTMRs, elucidate the
involvement of Aβ-HTMRs in trigeminal neuropathic pain manifested with orofacial mechanical allodynia and
underlying molecular mechanisms. This project is highly relevant to public health because it will provide
important insights into trigeminal neuropathic pain and novel therapeutic targets for treating this debilitating
pain disorder.

title: Targeting the Sexual Cycle of Pneumocystis
text:
The prevalence of health factors that compromise the immune systems of US veterans and
predispose them to infection with opportunistic pathogens like Pneumocystis is significant.
Besides infection with HIV, obesity in the US has increased over the past several decades.
Obesity is linked to more than 60 chronic diseases, including cancers. In 2014 (the most recent
update), the VA estimated that 78% of US veterans (including men, women and ethnic minorities)
were overweight or obese (Spotlight on Obesity, May 2020) rendering them susceptible to
cancers, other immune debilitating diseases, and opportunistic infections like Pneumocystis
pneumonia. Opioid drug overdoses of US military veterans have increased by 53% from 2010-
2019, establishing another susceptible veteran population who are often co-infected with HIV and
HCV.

title: Shock Patients: Interprofessional Communication to Enhance Diagnosis (SPICED)
text:
Differentiating between causes of shock in the 1.3 million Americans annually who develop
shock annually is extremely challenging and requires many clinical experts to provide their
perspective. Yet, there is no way for these clinicians to actively share their assessments, build a
shared understanding of the cause of shock, and reach a consensus on treatment. The
proposed resarch will understand why interprofessional clinicians disagree on the cause of
shock, and then design and test a systematic process for interprofessional clinicians to share
information, assessments and build a shared understanding of the cause of shock.

title: Molecular origins and evolution to treatment resistance in genitourinary cancers
text:
While many cancer genomics studies have opened novel biological paradigms for tumor-intrinsic dysregulation
resulting from treatment resistance and new translational impacts, the role of integrated somatic, germline, and
immune systems toward treatment resistance has not been fully characterized in GU cancers. With Research
Specialist Dr. Jihye Park's recent and ongoing contributions, our NCI funded research programs will continue to
conduct systematic and comprehensive investigations of somatic, germline, and immune cell components that
together drive cancer risk and selective response to existing and emerging therapies across GU cancers. Under
Unit Director Dr. Eliezer Van Allen's leadership, this interdisciplinary and highly collaborative group will continue
to drive these comprehensive clinical computational research programs by utilizing novel sequencing
approaches and computational methods, and by sharing these discoveries with the broader community to
synergize collaboration in the cancer genomics field.

title: Characterizing estrogen regulation of neuronal excitability in the extended amygdala
text:
Alcohol use disorder presents a significant level of comorbidity with mental health conditions such as anxiety
disorder, particularly among women. We find that high levels of estrogen during the estrous cycle correlate with
an increase in alcohol drinking, lower levels of anxiety, as well as increased activity in BNSTCRF neurons, a
population we have shown to mediate these behaviors. Investigating the link between these behaviors and
estrogenic signaling in these neurons will facilitate the development of more targeted treatments for alcohol use
and anxiety disorders.

title: Vaginal Microbiome, Inflammatory Mediators, Metabolome, and Dysmenorrhea Symptom-based Phenotypes
text:
Dysmenorrhea (characterized by menstrual pain) affects up to 95% of reproductive-age women, disrupts their
daily activities, and increases their risk for other chronic pain conditions. We propose to examine relationships
among vaginal microbiome, inflammatory mediators, metabolome, sex hormones, and individual differences in
dysmenorrhea symptoms. This study is expected to discover new evidence that could lead to expanded
treatment options for the most common gynecological pain condition.

title: Improving Brain Recovery Through Glycoengineering
text:
This project exploits a technology platform that modulates the activities and functions of neural stem cells by
biochemically engineering their cell surface carbohydrates. We apply this “metabolic glycoengineering”
strategy to promote neural regeneration to heal brain injury in a rodent model and investigate the mechanistic
basis of the anticipated healing effects.

title: Quantitative imaging of choroid plexus function and neurofluid circulation in Alzheimer's Disease Related Dementia
text:
Neurofluid circulation has gained much attention in light of its likely relevance to neurodegenerative and
cerebrovascular disorders, including but not limited to Alzheimer’s Disease Related Dementias (ADRDs).
Fundamental to the effective circulation of neurofluids is cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) production activity, which
occurs within the choroid plexus (ChP) complexes located within each of the four brain ventricles; despite this,
we lack rigorous and quantitative methods for quantifying ChP activity, thereby limiting abilities to evaluate CSF
circulation in different neurodegenerative disorders, as well as in response to emerging therapies. The overall
goal of this work is to refine and clinically evaluate neuroimaging methods to enable quantitation of ChP anatomy
and function non-invasively in vivo; if successful, this will allow for ChP function to be interrogated reliably in the
growing number of applications where neurofluid and CSF circulatory dysfunction are implicated.
